fact: India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.
Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
Defines 'the State' for the purpose of Fundamental Rights.
The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or equal protection of the laws.
Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
Protects six freedoms including speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession.
No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
Free and compulsory education for all children of the age of six to fourteen years.
Right to move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights; Dr. Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution.
The State shall organise village panchayats and endow them with self-government powers (DPSP).
The State shall endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens throughout India (DPSP).
Duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition, the standard of living and improve public health (DPSP).
Lists the Fundamental Duties of every citizen of India; added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
There shall be a President of India.
There shall be a Vice-President of India.
President can grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment, including in death-sentence cases.
Attorney General for India — the highest law officer of the Government of India.
Definition of a Money Bill; a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
The President causes the Annual Financial Statement (the Budget) to be laid before Parliament.
President can promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session and immediate action is necessary.
Establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court of India.
Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
The Governor of a State is appointed by the President.
Governor can promulgate ordinances when the State Legislature is not in session.
High Courts can issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.
President may establish an Inter-State Council to inquire into and advise on inter-state disputes and coordination.
President constitutes a Finance Commission every five years to recommend distribution of taxes between Centre and States.
Parliament can create new All-India Services, including an All-India Judicial Service.
Superintendence, direction and control of elections is vested in the Election Commission.
Proclamation of Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
If the President is satisfied that State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution, President's Rule can be imposed.
Proclamation of Financial Emergency if the financial stability or credit of India is threatened.
Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure for amendment.
